businesses.name: Bowne Barry & Barry, Attorneys at Law
businesses.what_they_do: Two-attorney firm defending New Jersey mental-health clinicians before their licensing boards (social work, LPC, LMFT, CADC, psychology) and advising on practice/ethics issues, consent orders, reinstatement and business matters. Also handles some general matters such as real-estate closings.
businesses.customers: Licensed mental-health professionals and group/agency practices regulated by the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs.

size_signals.signal: Two attorneys named: David C. Barry (JD Georgetown, also an LSW with MSW from Rutgers, past NASW-NJ president) and Laura Bowne Barry (Of Counsel)
Office at 5 Auer Court, Suite A, East Brunswick; single phone (732) 238-8686
New 2026-dated site build with hero images uploaded 2026/09, plus practice-area pages, FAQ and blog

listing.platform: Birdeye aggregate for East Brunswick legal services (Google Business Profile not verifiable)

website_review.primary_cta: 'REQUEST A CONSULTATION' button in the sticky header and hero; tel: number in the header
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: consultation request form (#contact) — no calendar or instant booking
website_review.trust_signals: Named attorneys with credentials and photos, board-by-board coverage tied to N.J.A.C. citations, 'How a board matter moves' process explainer, FAQ, blog, 13 reviews at 5.0 on an aggregator
website_review.out_of_date_signs: None observed; images and content are 2026 and the design is current
website_review.search_basics: Clear niche titles and headings about licensing-board defence, but no meta description on the home page and no LegalService/Attorney JSON-LD with the East Brunswick address
top_issues: No meta description on the home page (search snippet is uncontrolled)
Structured data is a generic WebPage graph — no LocalBusiness/Attorney node with address, phone, hours
No published hours and no online calendar for the free consultation
Firm contact email is a personal Gmail address (BowneBarry@gmail.com)

agent_readiness.notes: robots.txt is Yoast-default and fully permissive. The site is unusually answerable: real text about each board and N.J.A.C. section, a step-by-step process explainer, FAQ and blog. Bookable is close but limited to a form — no hours, no calendar, no confirmation agent; and the JSON-LD doesn't identify the business address.

operations_signals.signal: Firm markets 'personalized attention and responsiveness' with only two attorneys and no scheduling system — responsiveness claims depend on manual handling
Deadline-driven work ('administrative response windows move fast'), which makes intake triage and reminder automation high-value
13 reviews at 5.0 on an aggregator, so review volume is thin relative to a deliberate reputation push

top_opportunities.opportunity: Consultation booking with qualification (which board, complaint vs. inquiry, deadline date) so urgent board letters jump the queue
top_opportunities.evidence: Site stresses fast administrative deadlines; booking is a generic '#contact' form with no calendar or hours

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add Attorney/LegalService JSON-LD with the Auer Court address, phone, hours and board specialties, plus a proper meta description
top_opportunities.evidence: 0 LocalBusiness/Attorney nodes (only a WebPage graph) and no meta description on the home page

top_opportunities.opportunity: Licensing-board Q&A content plus an agent that screens inbound clinician questions and routes to the right service page
top_opportunities.evidence: Strong existing process/FAQ content and per-board pages, but no structured Q&A or after-hours capture

scores.reasons: Gap 2: modern, fast, clear niche with form and click-to-call; only metadata, schema and booking are missing. Pay 4: professional licensees facing career-risk matters, likely healthy fees. Ease 4: small two-partner firm, decisions are fast. Evidence 3: site inspected at both widths; review count and Google listing second-hand.

caveats: All ten businesses are law firms in East Brunswick; none fell into the excluded categories.

Google search and Google Maps could not be read from this machine (Google returned 'unusual traffic' bot checks), so no Google Business Profile rating, review count, claimed status, hours or category could be verified for any business. Ratings shown come from Avvo, Lawyers.com, BBB or Birdeye and are labelled as such.
Page <title> values returned through the browser carried a stray emoji prefix (a horse glyph) on several sites; treated as a browser artifact, not a site defect, and excluded from the findings.
Law firms rarely publish fees, so price ranges were generally not available; where 'no fee unless we recover' or 'free consultation' is stated it comes from the firm's own copy.
Scores are judgments about each business as observed today, not about the legal industry generally.
